question: Demonetisation was a new initiative taken by the Government of India in _______ to tackle the problem of corruption, black money, terrorism and circulation of fake currency in the economy.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tue Nov 01 2016 00:00:00 GMT+0530 (India Standard Time)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Demonetisation in India was announced on **November 8, 2016** by Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
 
• The initiative aimed to curb the widespread issues of **corruption, black money, terrorism financing, and the circulation of counterfeit currency**.
 
• The demonetisation involved the invalidation of ₹500 and ₹1000 banknotes as legal tender, which accounted for approximately **86% of the cash in circulation** at that time.
 
• New ₹500 and ₹2000 banknotes were introduced to replace the old currency, and citizens were required to exchange or deposit the old notes in banks within a specified period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Corruption**

 
 
• Corruption is the abuse of entrusted power for private gain. It can be classified as grand, petty, and political, depending on the amounts of money lost and the sector where it occurs.
 
• Corruption erodes trust, weakens democracy, hampers economic development and further exacerbates inequality, poverty, social division and the environmental crisis.
 
 
 
• **Black Money**
 
 
• Black money refers to funds earned on the black market, on which income and other taxes have not been paid. It is typically received in cash from underground economic activity and, as such, is not taxed.
 
• Black money is often used in illegal activities, such as crime, drug trade, terrorism, and corruption.
 
 
 
• **Terrorism Financing**
 
 
• Terrorism financing involves the solicitation, collection or provision of funds with the intention that they may be used to support terrorist acts or organizations.
 
• It is often done through a variety of methods, including money laundering, smuggling, and the exploitation of legitimate businesses and charities.
 
 
 
• **Fake Currency**
 
 
• Counterfeit money is imitation currency produced without the legal sanction of the state or government and designed to deceive the recipient into believing that it is genuine.
 
• Counterfeiting is a criminal activity that is often linked to other forms of crime, including money laundering, drug trafficking, and terrorism.
